First printed by the King's Printer Robert Barker, this was the third translation into English to be approved by the English Church authorities. The first was the Great Bible commissioned in the reign of King Henry VIII, and the second was the Bishops' Bible of 1568. In January 1604, King James I convened the Hampton Court Conference where a new English version was conceived in response to the perceived problems of the earlier translations as detected by the Puritans, a faction within the Church of England.
James gave the translators instructions intended to guarantee that the new version would conform to the ecclesiology and reflect the episcopal structure of the Church of England and its belief in an ordained clergy. The translation was done by 47 scholars, all of whom were members of the Church of England. In common with most other translations of the period, the New Testament was translated from Greek, the Old Testament was translated from Hebrew text, while the Apocrypha were translated from the Greek and Latin. In the Book of Common Prayer (1662), the text of the Authorized Version replaced the text of the Great Bible – for Epistle and Gospel readings – and as such was authorized by Act of Parliament. By the first half of the 18th century, the Authorized Version was effectively unchallenged as the English translation used in Anglican and Protestant churches. Over the course of the 18th century, the Authorized Version supplanted the Latin Vulgate as the standard version of scripture for English speaking scholars. Today, the most used edition of the King James Bible, and often identified as plainly the King James Version, especially in the United States, closely follows the standard text of 1769, edited by Benjamin Blayney at Oxford.

PUBNiTO is your single application for accessing your bookstore, creating and growing your library of purchased and personal books, and reading those books.
PUBNiTO is a modern and highly secure book reader for ePUB3, PDF, and Audio books. ePUB3 is optimal for an immersive reading experience on all types of devices and screen sizes. It gives plenty of possibilities, including Audio, Video, Interactivity, Multiple Language Support, Reflowable and Fixed Layouts, Accessibility and much more. This has made it ideal for modern educational books, including K12 and university textbooks, monographs, training manuals, procedures books, and any content that can be conveyed better via ePUB3 elements.

This version of the PUBNiTO supports PDF and Audio books in addition to ePUB3. All three formats are made highly secure through our DRM which is certified by the EDRLab.

PUBNiTO is free and can be used in two ways:

Public: If you prefer not to register and create an account, you are able to fully browse a bookstore which is associated with your application. It helps you read about them, and check their ratings and customer reviews. 

Personal: If you wish to buy books, read, annotate, highlight, bookmark, solve quizzes, and more, we invite you to create an account. This helps us keep your content safe.

You can add books to your personal library in two ways:

The most common way is to explore your store to sample, lease, or purchase your favourite ebooks from the book store website. Once you have acquired a book from the  store, then it is automatically added to your personal library and is available in this app.

Alternatively, you can upload your own digital books (as long as they are standard ePUB3, PDF, or Audio Book) to your personal library.

Online books can be in any language. PUBNiTO interface is available in a number languages and the list is always growing.

PUBNiTO is unique in supporting Right to Left languages such as Arabic. It fully supports true mathematical formulas and equations in any direction.

Start reading a book and it will remain available offline.
